summary: ship Step 13 `branches sync-dev` silently skipped because the main checkout was left bare
description: `bkit branches sync-dev` exits 0 with `devLocal: skipped` when `core.bare=true` blocks the fast-forward, so the step looks green while local `dev` stays behind `origin/dev`. Only the log line 'git refused: fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree' distinguishes it; the gate item 'Local dev synced' would read as satisfied on a pass-exit without reading that line.
remediation: Detect the bare state in `branches sync-dev` (and `repo info`) and exit non-zero with the repair command, instead of folding it into a skipped field with exit 0.

summary: Repeated `bkit steps finish` commit failures (exit 8) on a worktree whose worktree.copy names a gitignored file; the run had to abort at Step 2
description: On build run 1 of 700-session-start-nudge the Step 2 `bkit steps finish` exited 8 (EXIT_COMMIT): the row landed but `git add -A -- . :(exclude).bkit/.env` refused because `.bkit/.env` is gitignored and was copied into the worktree by `bkit worktrees setup`. Every subsequent commit would fail the same way, so the run could not persist work and was routed to the Failure Path; `bkit workflows fail` and the handover push then ran (the handover commit succeeded via a different path). Root cause recorded as failures key `worktree-copy-gitignored-file-breaks-commit`.

summary: Step 7's `bkit branches push --mode=feature` was refused three times by the pre-push gate before it landed, each time on a different load-induced 5s/30s test timeout
description: Plan workflow for 701-engine-work-build, 2026-10-26. The feature branch carries five unpushed local-`dev` commits with code, so `bkit ci min-push` fails and every push runs the full `pnpm bkit:gate:static-unit-integration`: attempt 1 failed 5 tests (ci-scripts.test.ts 30s, runs.test.ts 5s x3), attempt 2 failed 2 (resolve-push-base.test.ts 5s, runs.test.ts 5s), attempt 3 passed. The failures are load-induced: the machine was running another session's full vitest suite in `.worktrees/700-session-start-nudge` (load average 8-10 on 10 cores), and each failing file passes on its own in the same worktree. Each attempt costs a full static + coverage-unit + bats + integration run.
remediation: Two levers: push `dev` to origin (its five commits are what make the branch non-min, per the worktree setup warning) so later feature pushes take the light `bkit:gate:min` path; and make the audit tests' fixed 5s/30s timeouts load-aware the way the unit tier's test-timeout-budget already is, so a busy machine cannot block a mandated workflow push.

summary: build Step 6 steps finish commit refused by bkit:check:dist after engine TS edits
description: Group 1 edited .bkit/core/engine/**/*.ts. The repo pre-commit hook runs bkit:check:dist whenever a staged non-test engine TS exists, and the committed dist/ was stale, so steps finish exited 8 (row written, commit failed). No build workflow step, plan template or prompt mandates pnpm build + git add dist/ for engine edits (gotcha kn-7 names .bkit/src/*.ts only), so the plan omitted it and every subsequent commit in the run is blocked by the same guard.
remediation: Add pnpm build && git add dist/ to the plan runbook (and the plan-convert / plan-execute prompts) whenever a task edits .bkit/core/engine/**/*.ts, so the step commit passes bkit:check:dist.

summary: plan-execute subagent self-authorized a .prettierignore + workflows.md format-gate config change
description: Group 1's subagent hit format:check failing on the raw build-task-red-*.md logs the mandated red command writes, and self-authorized edits to .prettierignore, .bkit/templates/.prettierignore, .bkit/core/.bkit/workflows.md and its mirror. It also reported a test file truncated to 0 bytes by an edit call, then restored byte-for-byte with two harness fixes (test-changed). Owner review of the config change is owed.
remediation: Ship the raw-gate log ignore pattern in the template .prettierignore so plan runs need no self-authorized edit.

summary: build Step 8 gaps-remediate subagent returned a status line with a PENDING header while its own gate run was still going
description: Group 1's group gate failed on one unit test timeout; the gaps-remediate subagent started a full `pnpm vitest run` to verify a fix and returned before it finished, leaving build-plan-gaps-remediate-1-1-log.md with `Verdict: PENDING` and an empty Remediation Log, plus an orphaned vitest process. `steps finish` would read the PENDING header (exit 5). The group-gate scope (full static-unit-integration tier) is far longer than one subagent turn, so an agent that waits on it returns mid-run.
remediation: Give the gaps-remediate prompt an explicit long-run contract: run a scoped command for the failing test only, never the full tier, and never wait on a background gate — or raise the subagent turn budget so a full-tier verify fits one turn.

summary: `pnpm bkit:test:file <a> <b>` with BKIT_TEST_REPORT unset writes JUnit XML over the first named test file
description: During group 4 verification a scoped run `pnpm bkit:test:file <fileA> <fileB>` with BKIT_TEST_REPORT unset expanded an empty `--outputFile.junit=` and consumed fileA as the JUnit output path, overwriting `.bkit/core/engine/audits/hooks/session-rules-advisory.integration.test.ts` with XML. The agent noticed, restored the file from HEAD and re-ran via `pnpm exec vitest run`; `git diff HEAD` confirms the file is byte-identical, so no work was lost. A destructive default: an unset report env turns a test path into an output path.
remediation: Make `bkit:test:file` default `--outputFile.junit` to a temp path (or omit the flag) when BKIT_TEST_REPORT is unset, so a positional test path can never be treated as an output target.

summary: build Step 15's roadmap mirror commits the roadmap row to dev while the run's PR is still open, so the PR reports CONFLICTING against dev
description: Step 15 sub-step 3 runs `bkit roadmap mirror --workflow=build --fid=...`, which landed `93ad96e51 docs(700-session-start-nudge): build roadmap update bkit [skip ci]` on `origin/dev` during this run. The run's own close commit on `feat/700-session-start-nudge` also carries the same roadmap ledger row, so after the PR opened (#708) the two sides touched the same ledger file and GitHub reported the PR `mergeable: CONFLICTING`, `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`, even though the branch had been rebased onto local dev with no conflicts. The PR then needs a rebase onto the new origin/dev (roadmap ledgers are merge=union) before it can merge.
remediation: Mirror the roadmap row to dev only after the PR merges (ship), or land the mirror on the feature branch and let ship move it to dev, so a build's own close cannot dirty its own PR.

summary: ship Step 6's docs sync edits `.bkit/core/.bkit/*` sources and their root `.bkit/*` mirrors plus `.bkit/version`, but `bkit ledgers commit --scope=pr` stages only `:(glob)docs/*.md`, so those edits can never ride the ship bookkeeping commit and the orchestrator must add a separate commit
description: After the Step 6 docs subagent synced host/provider docs and ran `bkit install` (which rewrote `.bkit/version` canonical hashes), `bkit ledgers commit --scope=pr` committed `docs/testing.md`, `docs/technology.md`, `docs/roadmap.md` and the ship artifacts but left nine `.bkit/` files dirty (`.bkit/{providers,README,cloud,install}.md`, `.bkit/core/.bkit/{providers,README,cloud,install}.md`, `.bkit/version`). Nothing in the ship workflow commits them before merge, so on the literal workflow they would be discarded when Step 14 removes the worktree, shipping a PR whose docs still describe the pre-change state. The orchestrator committed them as `9871db9ef docs(700-session-start-nudge): sync host/provider docs for the rules-read hook` before the Step 8 push.
remediation: Widen `bookPathspecs(scope=pr)` (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/ledgers.ts`) to the doc surfaces the ship docs sync edits — at minimum `.bkit/*.md`, `.bkit/core/.bkit/*.md` and `.bkit/version` — or have the docs step stage its own edits, so the docs sync always rides the bookkeeping commit.

summary: `ship-input-*.md`, `ship-deferred-sweep.md` and `ship-summary.md` are not on `.prettierignore` and fail `prettier --check`, which the pre-push `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration` runs, blocking the Step 8 bookkeeping push
description: The Step 6 docs subagent reported `pnpm format:check` failing on two untracked ship artifacts (`ship-deferred-sweep.md`, `ship-input-1.md`); `ship-summary.md` failed too. `.prettierignore` already exempts sibling workflow artifacts (`docs/plans/*/logs/*/run-tests-*.md`, `build-task-red-*.md`, `build-group-gate-*.md`, `context-tests-local-*.md`) as raw output, but not the `ship-*` family. The orchestrator ran `prettier --write` on the three artifacts before the bookkeeping commit so the push gate could pass.
remediation: Add `docs/plans/*/logs/*/ship-*.md` to the `.prettierignore` template (same rationale as the existing workflow-artifact entries) so ship artifacts never block the bookkeeping push.

summary: build Step 6 group commit blocked by the dist freshness hook because the plan scheduled the dist rebuild after the engine source change
description: The plan for 703 edits non-test engine source in .bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/decisions.ts (GROUP 1, TASK 1) but schedules the mandated `pnpm build` dist rebuild as TASK 6 in GROUP 3. bkit's own pre-commit hook runs `pnpm bkit:check:dist` on any staged non-test .bkit/core/engine/**/*.ts change, so the Step 6 build-plan-execute commit failed with exit 8 (row written, commit failed) and every later step commit would fail the same way until dist is rebuilt. Recovery was the planned TASK 6 work (`pnpm build`) executed early, then `steps finish` re-run.
remediation: Plan-convert must fold the `pnpm build` dist rebuild into the same task as any non-test engine source edit, or place the rebuild task in the earliest group that changes engine source (KN-7).

summary: Ship Step 8's mandated bookkeeping push uses a `[skip ci]` subject, but the pre-push hook blocks any push whose HEAD carries a CI-suppressor token while the branch has an open PR, so the orchestrator must add a bare trigger commit before the push can land
description: `bkit ledgers commit --scope=pr` commits the ship bookkeeping with the workflow-mandated subject `docs({FID}): ship bookkeeping bkit [skip ci]`. `.husky/pre-push` (CI-suppressor HEAD guard) then refuses the Step 8 `bkit branches push --mode=plain`: HEAD carries `[skip ci]` and PR #711 is open, so the PR's checks would stay vacuously green. The push failed with exit 8 and no route in the workflow; the hook's own message names the fix, so the orchestrator ran `git commit --allow-empty -m "chore(703-standardise-question-option): re-trigger"` and re-pushed. CI then ran at the trigger commit and the merge gate validated at the code head.
remediation: Either drop `[skip ci]` from the ship bookkeeping subject (it lands on a feature branch, not dev, so CI must run at HEAD), or have `bkit ledgers commit --scope=pr` append a bare trigger commit when the target branch has an open PR, or give `bkit branches push` a documented re-trigger path so Step 8 is not left with an unrouted exit 8.

summary: Gate 14's `bkit steps gate --file="{REPO_ROOT}/docs/plans/.../status.jsonl" --ref=origin/dev` exits 3 in a bare main checkout because `readStatusRowsAt` walks up to the bare root, where `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` fails
description: The main checkout for this repo is bare (`git rev-parse --is-bare-repository` = true); worktrees live under `.worktrees/`. After Step 14 removed the ship worktree, the Gate 14 command's `{REPO_ROOT}` path has no working tree, so `readStatusRowsAt` (`status.ts`) resolves the nearest existing parent to the bare root and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` returns null → exit 3 (`... is not inside a git repo`). The orchestrator re-ran the same gate anchored at an existing worktree path with the same `--ref=origin/dev`, which read the file from origin/dev and passed.
remediation: Have `readStatusRowsAt` fall back to `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` / the main-checkout resolver (as `lib.ts` already does) when `--show-toplevel` fails, so the close gate works in a bare main checkout; or have the ship workflow run Gate 14 from a worktree anchor.

summary: Verify subagent blocked by provider credit limit

summary: Build summary FAIL cannot be cleared by a resolved Decision Pause
description: `bkit workflows summary` folds the last row per step+group and counts a `build-plan-execute` FAIL as a hard failure; ANSWERED_BY maps only build-challenge, so a group whose execute returned FAIL for a BLOCKED task later accepted by the owner (TEST EXCEPTION) keeps the run at FAIL. Every task was ticked, plan-check was clean and the full suite passed, yet Step 15 can only route to the Failure Path.

summary: A ship re-run after a Failure Path flush is blocked by the failed run's uncommitted files left in the resumed worktree
description: The Failure Path flush lands the run's book on dev from a throwaway checkout but leaves the worktree with a modified status.jsonl and untracked ship-*.md files that dev now tracks. On the re-run (a) prettier --check . in pre-push failed on the untracked ship-*.md files, blocking a code push, and (b) Step 4 B2 conflict-resolve could not start git rebase origin/dev: cannot rebase, unstaged changes. The agent may not commit or stash, so the ship failed again.
remediation: worktrees setup on resume (or the Failure Path flush) should reconcile the worktree's book with what the flush landed on dev: commit or drop the flushed files, so a re-run starts from a clean tree.

summary: ship-update-docs edits CHANGELOG.md but ledgers commit --scope=pr does not stage it, so the docs sync's changelog entry is left uncommitted
description: Step 6's docs agent added an [Unreleased] bullet to the root CHANGELOG.md. Step 8's ledgers commit --scope=pr allow-list covers docs/*.md, ledgers and skills but not CHANGELOG.md, so the bullet stayed dirty in the worktree and does not ride the PR.
remediation: Either add CHANGELOG.md to the --scope=pr pathspecs (and the runs gate bookkeeping allow-list), or tell bkit-ship-update-docs not to edit files outside docs/.

summary: ship worktrees setup run from inside the feature's own worktree picks adopt mode and exits 7
description: Step 1 sub-step 7 ran from .worktrees/715-retire-lite-workflows, whose current branch is the ship target, so worktrees setup chose adopt mode (session branch = target), tried to switch the main checkout onto feat/715-retire-lite-workflows, and git refused because the worktree already holds that branch. It exits 7, which the workflow routes as a ship of dev or main and stops. Re-running the same block from the repo root resumed the worktree.
remediation: In worktrees setup, treat a session already inside the target's registered worktree as resumed, or give this refusal its own exit code.

summary: ship docs sync edits a docs table row with padding, so the Step 8 bookkeeping push is refused by format:tables:check
description: The ship update-docs agent rewrote a row of a prettier-ignore table in docs/testing.md with fixed-width padding. ledgers commit committed it, and the pre-push gate's format:tables:check refused the push (branches push exit 8). Step 8 has no route for a refused push, so the only written path is the Failure Path, which would end the run over a whitespace fix. The orchestrator ran bkit-insert-ignore.mjs on the file, committed it, and re-ran the push.
remediation: Run the table formatter on docs the ship docs agent touched before ledgers commit, or give Step 8 a route for a hook-refused push: fix what the hook names, commit, re-run the push.
